title: Diabetes mellitus: type, complications and medication status
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's diabetes, its complications and related long-term drug use.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for diabetes management.

HPI
The patient is a 58-year-old male presenting for a routine follow-up regarding his type 2 diabetes mellitus. He reports that his blood glucose levels have been stable since his last visit. He continues to adhere to his long-term medication regimen and denies any acute concerns or recent episodes of illness. He reports no issues with weight gain or injection site reactions.

Medication List
- Insulin and metformin (long-term)

Exam
The patient appears well-nourished and in no acute distress. Skin is intact without lesions. Vital signs are stable.

Assessment
1. Type 2 diabetes mellitus, without complications.

Plan
The patient will continue his current long-term regimen of insulin and his oral hypoglycemic medication. We will continue to monitor his laboratory values at the next scheduled visit. The patient was instructed to maintain his current routine and report any changes in symptoms. Follow-up in three months.
explanations: No complication is documented: type 2 diabetes without complications.
When both insulin and oral hypoglycemics are used, assign both Z79.4 and Z79.84.

distractors.why: Nothing in the note documents hyperglycemia or poor control.
Both Z codes are assigned when both drug types are used.
